source_snapshot.test_name_items: UEFI Shell basic command - Boot OS
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Boot into OS via UEFI shell

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Boot into UEFI shell.
2. Go to boot partition via cmd: fs0
3. Execute grubx64.efi to boot into OS via cmd: /boot/efi/EFI/ubuntu/grubx64.efi
Criteria:
1.  System should be able to boot into OS from UEFI shell.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- UEFI Shell basic command - Boot OS: UEFI Shell `Boot OS` command boots an OS from the UEFI shell; requires pre-OS interactive control to select the boot target.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator boots the OS from the UEFI shell + records the boot; agent cannot drive the pre-OS shell.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO; correctly identifies the pre-OS interactive boundary but omits path identity, post-boot target proof and recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds valuable target/path/post-boot controls but treats an automatable after-check as if the core manual EFI launch were only setup.
historical_reviews.round_02: No additional exact-code technical record found.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: No V3/V3.1 record exists for this variant.

original_test_intent: From the UEFI Shell, select the correct EFI filesystem and manually launch the approved installed OS bootloader, then verify that the intended OS—not an installer or another disk—boots successfully.
original_method: Map the approved EFI system partition, boot the shell, select the mapped filesystem, launch the verified EFI binary, capture the console transition, collect OS/root/UEFI health evidence, and restore the normal boot path.
manual_activity: A human must identify/select the filesystem in pre-OS UEFI Shell and launch the EFI binary. Agent post-boot checks assist evidence but do not perform this core acceptance operation.
required_inputs: EFI partition GUID/device and shell mapping
safety_requirements: Do not assume `fs0` is the target partition or that the Ubuntu path exists.
Do not launch an unidentified EFI binary, installer or recovery image.
Confirm the installed OS and alternate normal boot before shell entry.
Stop on ambiguous mapping, unexpected image or loss of console/OOB access.
Verify the intended root disk after boot and leave boot entries unchanged unless approved.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only EFI partition/boot-entry/OS identity evidence before execution.
After the human launch, verify OS, root disk, UEFI mode and health.
Correlate evidence without claiming the manual launch or final verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve filesystem mapping, exact EFI binary and recovery.
Perform/capture the UEFI Shell selection and launch.
Confirm intended OS boot and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It correctly preserves human pre-OS control but names no exact command or mapping.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the source fs0 and /boot/efi/EFI/ubuntu/grubx64.efi as original examples; execute them only when the actual shell mapping and binary identity match, otherwise use a project-approved equivalent without rewriting master coverage.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: fs0, Ubuntu grubx64.efi path, no-script state and 10/10-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map the EFI partition by stable disk/GPT identity, verify the bootloader path/binary owner, record the exact shell mapping and capture post-boot OS/root identity.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact installed OS and UEFI topology.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, shell, bootloader and OS versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner boot recipe and installed OS EFI layout.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds stable target identity and post-boot proof without substituting the manual shell launch.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: UEFI filesystem numbers can change between boots and are not stable identifiers.

project_override_considerations: Projects may provide a non-Ubuntu approved path and actual filesystem number. Completion applies to that plan only and must not claim the literal example path was tested if it was not.
expected_evidence: Platform/OS identity and approved EFI mapping
Shell capture showing selected filesystem and exact binary launch
Post-boot OS, root disk and UEFI-mode evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requires OS boot from UEFI Shell. The fixed filesystem/path are platform-specific inputs that must be validated, not contradictory facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is clear. Missing target/path/console/recovery affects readiness rather than permanent classification.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps its manual boundary and adds exact target/proof requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its strong safety and post-boot evidence but reclassifies to MANUAL ONLY because the EFI launch is core, not merely preparation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates supporting automation and engineer verdict under the locked core-activity rule.

review_improvement: Prevents volatile fs0 numbering or a distro-specific path from sending the host into an unintended boot environment while preserving the original example.
independent_technical_reasoning: Successful OS-side checks happen only after the decisive manual shell filesystem selection and EFI launch. Since that manual action is the function under test, V3.1 classifies the case MANUAL ONLY rather than PARTIAL.
no_automatic_retry: Do not try another filesystem or EFI binary automatically after failure; preserve the console state and obtain engineer disposition.
